::: {.callout-note}
**This page is for the facilitator.** It is left out of the navbar, so nothing on the site links to it. The track pages under `tracks/` are participant-facing and contain no instructor guidance, which is collected here and in the run sheets of the [facilitator guide of the case study](guide.qmd).
:::

## The formats

The facilitator chooses the format, and the link sent to the participants of a delivery leads to it, while the Formats section of the opening page is the way in to every format. Each track is an ordered route through pages of the site, with a docked sidebar of its own (`_sidebar.yml`) that lists its pages and the tools that it uses, an exercise page that sets out its tasks, and a slides page embedding the deck on which it runs. Each part page of a track carries the instructions for that part, with buttons into the page where the work is done, and the previous and next links at its foot follow the order of the sidebar. The timings are kept in the run sheets of the facilitator guide, and the participant pages give none, apart from the total of each stage of the independent format. Name the track of a delivery in `delivery.track` of `_variables.yml`, and the callout of the opening page links it; the navbar then shows a participant the last track page that they opened.

| Format | Track | Deck |
|---|---|---|
| Short format, browser only | `tracks/short/` | `live/short.qmd` |
| Day format | `tracks/day/` | `live/day.qmd` |
| long format | `tracks/long/` | the decks of day 1 on the AR4DS site, `live/day.qmd` on day 2, and the decks of day 3 |
| Self-study | `tracks/independent/` | `live/day.qmd` |

**What the day format holds.** The three one-day focuses of October 2026 (open science, data tools, methods) were merged into one workshop on 6 November 2026, in four parts: the claim and credibility, with SCORE and its robustness study (Multi100; Aczel et al. 2026) in brief; the estimand and the causal graph; the reproduction; and robustness, which holds the menu, the class chart with its submissions, the curve of the claim, the replication and the declared analysis. The tools are taught by the modules of the AR4DS site before the day, and live on the first day of the long format. The participants of the day format do the tasks in the workspace, in their IDE, and the live deck of the day shows each step with its output and stands in, with the browser lab, when an installation fails.

## The browser lab

The browser lab is a page that runs R in the tab of the browser and holds the five tasks of the exercise beside the workspace. It is live: it loads the data of the case study, about 100 KB of emails, and runs the code of the tasks on them, each fit in a fraction of a second. The live decks carry the same cells on their slides, with the same helpers, which are one file, `_includes/_lab-helpers.qmd`, beside the graph helpers of Task 2 in `_includes/_lab-graph.qmd`, and the lab is the fallback of both decks. The causal-graph task prints the answers that the pipeline computed with dagitty for the graphs that the cell offers, because dagitty cannot run in the tab; any other graph goes to the workspace.

## The decks

The live decks of the short format and of the day format, `live/short.qmd` and `live/day.qmd`, are assembled from the segments of `live/_segments/`, of which those with `-live` in their names carry the cells of the browser lab. The four decks of day 3 of the long format are assembled in `slides/` from the segments of `slides/_segments/day-3/`. Every deck starts from the two setup segments in `slides/_segments/shared/` and `slides/_segments/case/`: the shared one names no case study, and the setup chunk of the case study comes after it and gives the shared segments the addresses of the case study. The live decks have a folder of their own, because the `revealjs` key of `slides/_metadata.yml` would render a live deck twice, and `live/_metadata.yml` carries the same options under `live-revealjs`, with a style block that bounds the height of cell outputs. A deck is a list of `{{< include >}}` lines with its own agenda, aims and part dividers.

**How the optional runs are switched.** In the segment files, every slide of an optional run is marked with `.deepdive` and a `run` attribute (`tools`, `r`, `methods`, `multiverse`). A deck lists the runs that belong to its main flow under `core-runs:` in its YAML, and `slides/core-runs.lua` strips the `.deepdive` mark from those headings, so `nav-tools.html` neither hides them on the `d` key nor badges them as optional. A run that is not listed stays optional: it is hidden in lean mode and has the escape-hatch link on its first slide.

**Why no segment is included twice in one deck.** The segment files contain R chunks with labels, and knitr refuses a duplicate label, so each deck includes each segment at most once.

**Rebuilding a deck.** Edit the segment files for content, or the deck file for order and framing, and render the deck on its own (`quarto render live/short.qmd`). A change to a segment needs every deck that includes it rendered again (`grep -l "_x.qmd" live/*.qmd slides/*.qmd`). The project render fails at its final move step on this machine, so decks are rendered one at a time.

## Housing and racial bias {#housing-and-racial-bias}

The Housing case study is taught in the short format, in the day format, and in the long format, whose second day is the day format. The short format runs in its live deck alone, in two halves, with the browser lab as the fallback: nothing is installed, nothing is sent to the class chart and nothing is preregistered. The day format is worked in the workspace, with the live deck showing each step and standing in, with the browser lab, when an installation fails. In Task 3 each participant chooses which of the analysts to reproduce; the four who recorded a statistic reproduce exactly from the public file, and P9W8Y, who recorded none, can be rerun but not matched. The [run sheet of the case study](guide.qmd) has the timings of the short format, of the day format and of the long format, the preparation that each format asks of participants, the expected numbers, the checks before the day and the order of what to cut.

## Self-study

The independent format takes the Housing case study in five stages, with the companion modules between the tasks, and ends on a project of each participant's own; a semester course can follow the same route in class. Its pages contain their own compression notes, written to the reader, because no facilitator is there to apply them, and each stage page gives the total of its stage and nothing finer. What the facilitator can still do for a self-study cohort is keep the live results pipeline running between deliveries, so that a result submitted alone appears on the Class results page of the case study ([`facilitator/live-results-setup.md`](https://github.com/CodeMoreh/ar4ds-eu/blob/main/facilitator/live-results-setup.md) in the repository of the site of the Europeanisation and the economy case study).

**The class chart.** The chart of the case study is on its Class results page, and it reads only the rows of this case study from the results Form shared by the case studies of the course. The labels of the Housing case study carry the word `housing` after the tag (`explore: [amber-otter-42] housing …`). The workspace keeps its tag in `.class-tag`, so ask a cohort to choose one nickname and to pass it as `nickname = "..."` every time. The chart keeps the rows of earlier deliveries until the sheet is cleared.
